text: Four-quarter GBV conversion gives an auditable guidance path. The current evidence supports scenario analysis; it does not establish a short or predict a share-price move.
+$18m / +0.58% versus a like-for-like Yahoo/LSEG implied-guide proxy. A lower guide than Street revenue is not itself a bearish surprise. [1, 2]

USD millions. Q3'26 actual issued guide: $4,690-4,770m; midpoint $4,730m [1]. Its modeled guide is a diagnostic, not an unknown forecast. Quarterly Q1/Q2'27 Street revenue and all direct guide-expectation panels are unavailable in the reviewed register.

R = conversion x (2/3 x prior-quarter GBV + 1/3 x two-quarter-prior GBV); G = R / (1 + cushion). Conversion is same-season EWM, two-year half-life; cutoff 13 Sep, n=5/5/6/6. Cushion is the prior eight observations' median, 1.7905%. Q3/Q4 GBV assumptions were component-derived; Q1'27 GBV is inherited and unvalidated. No second RNPL haircut. [2]
Yahoo 13 Sep: revenue $3,161.0m, n=36; S&P 10 Sep: $3,160m; Zacks 11 Sep: $3,200m. DoltHub mirrors Zacks; Yahoo/Alpha Vantage share the LSEG family. The sign is panel-sensitive. [2]
W1: 2023Q1-2026Q2; W2: 2024Q1-2026Q2, nested. Midpoint +/-$0.5m convention; raw RMSE $63.9m/$64.1m. Audit candidate uses ex-COVID conversion: different variant/origin from this EWM path. [3]

Errors move together. W2 Shapley component variances sum to 7,759.7; covariance contributes -3,662.7, leaving total variance 4,097.0 (USDm squared). Raw ex-post actual-GBV oracle RMSE is $36.4m/$38.7m (W1/W2); it is unavailable before release. Attribution is accounting, not causality. [3]

Short boundary, not a trade trigger: fixing the chosen panel and other inputs, Q4 conversion below 11.971% (base 12.040%) or Q3 GBV below $25,780.3m (base $26,008.6m) puts our guide below the proxy. A trade still needs robust expectations, uncertainty and executable returns.

Large earnings moves are real, but daily OHLC cannot reveal their intraday order or cause. All 23 ledger events are shown, including events with missing usable consensus; no large-move subsample is selected. [4]

23 events; 20 numeric first guides; 16 usable original revenue-consensus comparisons; 15 with a prior-data cushion. Across 12 primary tests (two expectation proxies x two daily legs x all/W1/W2 print windows), every Holm-adjusted p-value is 1.00. This neither proves zero effect nor establishes a tradeable guide-surprise rule. W1/W2 event proxy n=13/9. [4]
Use only the frozen early-origin prediction and contemporaneous expectations. Bear the entire origin-to-event return. Reconstruction is not an archived live signal.
The guide and call are public; the overnight gap is already gone. Test only returns available after entry, with costs and a rule fixed before evaluation.
Requires timestamped bars and exact publication, call start/end clocks. Held daily data cannot certify fills, wick order, stop execution or a call-only move.

What would strengthen a short? A dated, direct guide-expectation panel; a GBV or conversion downside that survives credible vendor/cushion choices; and a preregistered, net-of-cost entry test. RNPL cancellation/timing risk needs matched evidence before a numerical haircut.

What would falsify it? Net realized growth and conversion holding up through rollout laps; a guide consistent with the market's actual expectations; or a negative guide surprise that fails to predict returns available after the chosen entry. The present $18m Q4 gap is not a calibrated probability.

Immediate work: refresh the named expectation panel at the decision time; validate the conditional future GBV inputs; obtain ABNB+QQQ timestamped intraday history only if a call-entry trade is pursued. November 5 is a project expected date, not an official future schedule verified here. Daily gaps include the release, call, overnight and premarket.
